grand_strategy.reading: Samoa is a small state whose security sits in a 1962 treaty with New Zealand, whose money comes from remittances and from Australian and Chinese lending, and whose labour schemes send thousands of its people to work in New Zealand and Australia. The 2025 crisis changed who governs without changing that frame: Fiame Naomi Mataafa's government lost its budget vote on 27 May 2025, a snap election on 29 August gave FAST 30 seats (31 with a later defector) out of 51, and the FAST faction led by Laauli Leuatea Schmidt, which had split from Mataafa earlier in 2025, became the government on 16 September. At the UN the atlas records yes votes on all six Ukraine landmark resolutions from 2022 to 2026 and an abstention on the September 2024 resolution ending Israel's presence in the occupied Palestinian territory. The stage is the Commonwealth summit that Samoa hosted in Apia in October 2024, and no sourced foreign-policy line from the Schmidt government has been found beyond its March 2026 dispute with New Zealand over a matai title.

stances.note: Aligned by necessity, with visible friction. Samoa keeps no armed forces, and the 1962 Treaty of Friendship makes New Zealand the channel for defence help, so the alignment is structural. Friction is recurrent: the Western Samoa Citizenship Act 1982 overrode a 1982 Privy Council ruling for Samoans born 1924-1949, and NZ law restored that right on 20 Nov 2024; the Manawanui wreck off Upolu (Oct 2024) left a compensation grievance; and in March 2026 Samoa's prime minister said Luxon had sought a matai title, which Luxon's office denied and Apia later confirmed he had not requested. Not graded 'ally': Fiji's card reads its NZ framework as partnership, and Samoa's treaty is closer to alliance than that, so the call is a judgement and is marked B. Stable: the treaty holds, the friction recurs. Bond - affinity: 182,721 people of Samoan ethnicity lived in NZ at the 2018 census (Stats NZ, as cited on Wikipedia): affinity with a large diaspora, not kinship with the state.

stances.note: Partner, not ally: no defence treaty with Australia. The relation is aid, policing and labour mobility. Australia's 2025-26 budget set a record A$2.2bn for Pacific development (Samoan press report). Samoa's flagship programmes: Tautai (governance, A$45m, 2022-30) and Tautua (human development, A$40m, 2021-29), plus A$105.5m direct budget support and A$30m toward a Legislative Assembly building. Policing: the Samoa-Australia Policing Partnership turned 15 in 2024; the Nafanua III patrol boat was handed over in Nov 2023; the Pacific Policing Initiative made its first deployment at the Apia CHOGM. Labour: Samoa joined Australia's Pacific Labour Scheme in 2018 (Nauru Forum), reviewed its take-up in 2021 and capped contracts at three years; in Feb 2026 Wong said Samoa sets the numbers. Stable. Bond - affinity: Pacific and Commonwealth ties and a large diaspora, not kinship.

stances.note: Partner, transactional: no alignment, pure interest. Diplomatic relations date from 1976 (Wikipedia); another line on the same page says Samoa recognised the PRC from 1975, so the start date is not settled. Warming: the May 2022 agreement signed by Mataafa and Wang Yi covered climate change, COVID-19 and security; in Feb 2025 China gave WST$50,000 (NZ$30,000) to Safata villages after the Manawanui wreck. Money: China was owed $299.8m of $810.4m external debt at end-2023, about 37% (our calculation). Police: the 2025 police cooperation named in the brief is NOT confirmed. The only 2025 item found is a multilateral China-Pacific police dialogue (Lianyungang, 18 Sept 2025) that does not say Samoa signed anything. What exists: the 2022 pact, which SBS reported as including a fingerprint laboratory and talks on a police training centre (not opened), and the Dec 2023 Beijing dialogue where China offered law-enforcement and security cooperation. Chinese-built buildings: the eight-storey government office block on Apia's waterfront (1992-94, Chinese soft loan, shown on the $50 tala note per CGTN); a Mulinu'u justice and parliament-office complex under a Chinese loan (RNZ, not opened). Bond - none.

stances.note: Partner, light: cordial relations, formal diplomatic relations since 14 July 1971 (recognition on independence, 1 January 1962), the largest export market at nearly half of exports (per the US Embassy, as summarised in a search result), a Peace Corps programme since 1967, an embassy in Apia since 1988, and a 2012 shiprider agreement letting Samoan officers ride US Coast Guard ships. The American Samoa tuna cannery at Pago Pago (StarKist) draws on Samoan labour: about 1,700 workers at the January 2026 restart, per a trade-press report not checked against the company. The 2023-25 engagement asked for in the brief was NOT found in any source opened here. The US Embassy page refused the fetch (HTTP 403), so it is cited as the official page only, not as read. Stable. Bond - none: no kinship or grievance claim in the sources used.

The first dated source on the pair is the 2022 visit, so since 2022-11 is a floor, not the start of the tie. Stable.
